title: Post-Independence Consolidation
subject: History (CDS/NDA)

blocks.heading: 🇮🇳 Post-Independence Consolidation
blocks.intro: The challenges of nation-building, border demarcations, princely states integration, and linguistic reorganization after 1947.

blocks.heading: 1. Integration of Princely States
blocks.intro: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel (Minister of States) and V.P. Menon successfully integrated 549 princely states. Three states presented exceptions:
bullets: Junagadh: Nawab wanted to join Pakistan, but the Hindu majority population rebelled. Integrated via **Plebiscite (February 1948)**.
Hyderabad: Nizam refused to join India. Nizam's irregular militia (Razakars) terrorized the population. Integrated via military action code-named **Operation Polo (September 1948)**.

Jammu & Kashmir: Ruler Hari Singh wanted to remain independent. In October 1947, Pakistani armed tribal raiders invaded. Hari Singh signed the **Instrument of Accession (26 Oct 1947)**, and Indian troops flew in to defend Srinagar.

blocks.heading: 2. States Reorganization
bullets: Andhra Pradesh became the **first linguistic state** in 1953 following the death of Potti Sriramulu after a 56-day hunger strike.
**Dhar Commission (1948)** and **JVP Committee (1948 - Jawaharlal, Vallabhbhai, Pattabhi)** rejected language as basis of states.

Following Sriramulu's death, the government appointed the **Fazl Ali Commission (States Reorganization Commission, 1953)**. Its recommendations led to the **States Reorganization Act (1956)**, creating 14 states and 6 Union Territories.

formulas: Operation Polo: Hyderabad (1948) | 1st Linguistic State: Andhra (1953) | SRC 1956: Fazl Ali Commission
